  • Guides · MultipleNotes on "Building always-on agents": they look always on but mostly sleepThe author summarizes the article "Building always-on agents": an always-on agent sleeps most of the time, runs once when an event arrives, saves state and sleeps again. Five parts: Event Inbox (every trigger writes to a durable queue), Timers (separately stored follow-ups and schedules), Memory (persistent storage independent of sessions), Permissions, and Outbox. The loop: event into inbox → worker starts a run and creates or resumes a session → agent loads memory, acts within permissions, updates memory → result goes to outbox → dispatcher delivers; timers or user replies send new events back to the inbox. The author sees it as a blueprint similar to Grok Bot and Muse.vikingmute2026-11-15
